44	// not a fixed address. Scheme D parks it just above the program's declared
45	// RAM (the driver maps one page more than --mem-size), so no program layout
46	// can collide with it. This is the single source of truth for the GUEST
47	// address the Program-Buffer sweep (ResumeDriver/StateDrain) loads/stores
48	// through; the host stager below copies span-relative and needs no base.
49	inline constexpr auto v_scratch_gpa(uint64_t ram_base, std::size_t ram_size)
50	  -> uint64_t
51	{
52	  return ram_base + static_cast<uint64_t>(ram_size) - kVScratchBytes;
53	}
54	
55	// Sentinel for "no V scratch configured". ResumeDriver/StateDrain default to
56	// it; a non-V handoff never consults the scratch GPA, so that is fine, but if
57	// a V handoff reaches the sweep with the GPA still unset the driver throws
58	// (loud) rather than silently transporting V through a bogus address.
59	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpaUnset =
60	  static_cast<uint64_t>(-1);
61	
62	// GPR block-load prototype: x1..x31 (8 bytes each) staged in the TOP of the
63	// scratch page so the resume ld-sweep reads them below the V region (which
64	// grows up from the base). Reusing the V page keeps this single-repo; it only
65	// applies when the V data leaves room (gpr_scratch_fits), else the caller falls
66	// back to per-register abstract writes. A production version would give the GPR
67	// block its own scratch page instead of sharing the V one.
68	inline constexpr std::size_t kGprScratchBytes = 31 * 8;  // x1..x31
69	
70	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
71	{
72	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
73	}
74	
75	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
76	{
77	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
78	}
79	
80	// FPR block-load: f0..f31 (8 bytes each) staged just BELOW the GPR block. Unlike
81	// x0, f0 is a real register, so all 32 f-regs ride the sweep (kFprScratchBytes =
82	// 32*8, not 31*8). The two blocks are disjoint and staged up front, so the FPR
83	// fld-sweep (early in resume) and the GPR ld-sweep (later) never collide. The V
84	// region grows up from the base, so the fit gate here is tighter than the GPR
85	// one -- V must clear both blocks.
86	inline constexpr std::size_t kFprScratchBytes = 32 * 8;  // f0..f31
87	
88	inline constexpr auto fpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
89	{
90	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes;
91	}
92	
93	inline constexpr auto fpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
94	{
95	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb
96	         <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes;
97	}

預設**不是**。GPR/FPR restore 預設走 **Abstract Command**(DMI 一次寫一個 register),不占記憶體。PB block-sweep 是 **opt-in**、預設關掉的(`gpr_block_load_ = false` / `fpr_block_load_ = false`,`resume_driver.hpp:566-567`)。只有呼叫 `set_gpr_block_load(true)` / `set_fpr_block_load(true)` 才會改用 PB。

開啟後,才會像 Vector 一樣要占記憶體 -- 而且**沒有另外開 page,是共用 V 的那塊 scratch page**(mmap 最上面那一頁,`v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + ram_size - kVScratchBytes`)。

目前的分配(`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:62-97`),在那一頁 4KB 裡(`kVScratchBytes = 32 * 128 = 4096`):

```
高位址 ┌──────────────────────────────┐  page top
       │ GPR block  31*8 = 248 bytes  │  x1..x31 (x0 不算)   <- gpr_scratch_gpa
       │ FPR block  32*8 = 256 bytes  │  f0..f31 (32 個全上)  <- fpr_scratch_gpa
       │            ... gap ...        │
       │ V data     32 * vlenb        │  從 base 往上長
低位址 └──────────────────────────────┘  page base = v_scratch_gpa
```

重點:
- **三塊不重疊**。GPR 貼在頁頂,FPR 貼在 GPR 下面,V data 從頁底往上長。
- **有 fit gate**。只有 V data 塞得下、還留得出空間時才會用 PB:
  - `gpr_scratch_fits`: `32*vlenb <= 4096 - 248`
  - `fpr_scratch_fits`: `32*vlenb <= 4096 - 248 - 256`(比 GPR 更緊,因為 V 要讓出兩塊)
  - 塞不下就自動 fallback 回 per-register 的 abstract write。

一句話:這是原型作法,借用 V 的 page。程式碼註解自己也寫了 "A production version would give the GPR block its own scratch page instead of sharing the V one"(`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:66-67`),正式版應該給 GPR/FPR 各自獨立的 scratch page。

1	// V-register transport staging: the host<->guest-RAM half of the V data
2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores the V scratch region of guest
8	// RAM -- the top page of the mapped span (v_scratch_gpa, L26); this header
9	// provides the matching host-side copy:
10	//
11	//   - stage_v_to_scratch: state.vreg[] -> scratch RAM, called before resume so
12	//     the ResumeDriver vle8.v sweep reads QEMU 1's V values.
13	//   - read_v_from_scratch: scratch RAM -> state.vreg[], called after the
14	//     StateDrain vse8.v sweep so the drained v0..v31 land in state.vreg[]
15	//     (the handoff file).
16	//
17	// The transfer is transparent to the workload: benchmark binaries issue no
18	// transport code, only the enter_vsim / exit_vsim markers. rt_c_v_regs.c is
19	// the reference fixture.
20	//
21	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus. Easy to unit-test.
22	
23	#pragma once
24	
25	#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"
26	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
27	
28	#include <cstddef>
29	#include <cstdint>
30	#include <cstring>
31	#include <span>
32	#include <stdexcept>
33	
34	namespace hybrid
35	{
36	
37	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to the
38	// maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`. Defined in
39	// the shared ABI (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES) so the driver's mmap sizing and this
40	// consumer agree on one count (L26/F2).
41	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes = HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;
42	
43	// L26: the scratch region is the TOP kVScratchBytes of the mapped RAM span,
44	// not a fixed address. Scheme D parks it just above the program's declared
45	// RAM (the driver maps one page more than --mem-size), so no program layout
46	// can collide with it. This is the single source of truth for the GUEST
47	// address the Program-Buffer sweep (ResumeDriver/StateDrain) loads/stores
48	// through; the host stager below copies span-relative and needs no base.
49	inline constexpr auto v_scratch_gpa(uint64_t ram_base, std::size_t ram_size)
50	  -> uint64_t
51	{
52	  return ram_base + static_cast<uint64_t>(ram_size) - kVScratchBytes;
53	}
54	
55	// Sentinel for "no V scratch configured". ResumeDriver/StateDrain default to
56	// it; a non-V handoff never consults the scratch GPA, so that is fine, but if
57	// a V handoff reaches the sweep with the GPA still unset the driver throws
58	// (loud) rather than silently transporting V through a bogus address.
59	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpaUnset =
60	  static_cast<uint64_t>(-1);
61	
62	// GPR block-load prototype: x1..x31 (8 bytes each) staged in the TOP of the
63	// scratch page so the resume ld-sweep reads them below the V region (which
64	// grows up from the base). Reusing the V page keeps this single-repo; it only
65	// applies when the V data leaves room (gpr_scratch_fits), else the caller falls
66	// back to per-register abstract writes. A production version would give the GPR
67	// block its own scratch page instead of sharing the V one.
68	inline constexpr std::size_t kGprScratchBytes = 31 * 8;  // x1..x31
69	
70	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
71	{
72	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
73	}
74	
75	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
76	{
77	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
78	}
79	
80	// FPR block-load: f0..f31 (8 bytes each) staged just BELOW the GPR block. Unlike
81	// x0, f0 is a real register, so all 32 f-regs ride the sweep (kFprScratchBytes =
82	// 32*8, not 31*8). The two blocks are disjoint and staged up front, so the FPR
83	// fld-sweep (early in resume) and the GPR ld-sweep (later) never collide. The V
84	// region grows up from the base, so the fit gate here is tighter than the GPR
85	// one -- V must clear both blocks.
86	inline constexpr std::size_t kFprScratchBytes = 32 * 8;  // f0..f31
87	
88	inline constexpr auto fpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
89	{
90	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes;
91	}
92	
93	inline constexpr auto fpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
94	{
95	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb
96	         <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes;
97	}
98	
99	// CSR block (v3/v4): the Andes V5 + M-ext CSRs the sweep transports through the
100	// Program Buffer ride a scratch region just BELOW the FPR block. Sized to hold
101	// the MAX possible set (every defined CSR); the live count is smaller (flag- and
102	// caps-gated) and packs contiguously from slot 0. Slots = 13 Andes scalars + PMA
103	// (2 pmacfg + 16 pmaaddr) + 51 M-ext, auto-counted from the shared X-macros so
104	// the size never drifts as CSRs are added.
105	inline constexpr std::size_t kCsrScratchSlots = [] {
106	  std::size_t n = 0;
107	#define X(field, addr, name) ++n;
108	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
109	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
110	#undef X
111	  return n + HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM;
112	}();
113	inline constexpr std::size_t kCsrScratchBytes = kCsrScratchSlots * 8;
114	
115	inline constexpr auto csr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
116	{
117	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes
118	         - kCsrScratchBytes;
119	}
120	
121	inline constexpr auto csr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
122	{
123	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb
124	         <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes
125	              - kCsrScratchBytes;
126	}
127	
128	namespace detail
129	{
130	
131	// Byte offset of the scratch region inside a RAM span: its top page. Throws
132	// if the span is smaller than one scratch page (a too-small RAM mapping).
133	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size) -> std::size_t
134	{
135	  if (ram_size < kVScratchBytes)
136	    throw std::runtime_error(
137	      "v_regfile_xfer: RAM span smaller than the V scratch page");
138	  return ram_size - kVScratchBytes;
139	}
140	
141	}  // namespace detail
142	
143	// Walk every CSR the sweep transports, in canonical order -- Andes scalars, PMA
144	// ADDR, PMA CFG, then M-ext -- gated by the live block flag AND engine caps.
145	// Invokes fn(slot_index, csr_addr, field_ref) per transported CSR: the host
146	// stage copies field->scratch, the host lift copies scratch->field, and the
147	// ResumeDriver/StateDrain build their PB sweep's addr list -- all walking THIS
148	// identical order, so scratch slot i and csrs[i] always agree. State is
149	// templated so it binds const (stage / restore) and mutable (lift). PMA addr
150	// precedes cfg because the restore's TOR/NAPOT cfg consumes the addr already in
151	// place (mirrors the PMP/PMA restore ordering). Applies the same `(flags & FLAG)
152	// && caps.supports_csr(addr)` predicate every consumer of the block uses, so the
153	// single X-macro keeps them in lockstep.
154	template<typename State, typename Fn>
155	inline void for_each_sweep_csr(State& state, const AndesCaps& caps, Fn&& fn)
156	{
157	  std::size_t i = 0;
158	  if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES) {
159	#define X(field, addr, name) \
160	  if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) { fn(i, uint16_t(addr), state.andes.field); ++i; }
161	    HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
162	#undef X
163	    for (int p = 0; p < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM; ++p)
164	      if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + p)) {
165	        fn(i, uint16_t(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + p), state.andes.pmaaddr[p]); ++i;
166	      }
167	    for (int p = 0; p < HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM; ++p)
168	      if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * p)) {
169	        fn(i, uint16_t(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2 * p), state.andes.pmacfg[p]); ++i;
170	      }
171	  }
172	  if (state.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT) {
173	#define X(field, addr, name) \
174	  if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) { fn(i, uint16_t(addr), state.m_ext.field); ++i; }
175	    HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
176	#undef X
177	  }
178	}
179	
180	// Copy state.vreg[] into the span's top scratch page. Called just before vsim
181	// resumes the hart so the fixture can vle8.v from scratch and pick up QEMU 1's
182	// V values.
183	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
184	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram)
185	{
186	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
187	  // Pack at vlenb stride (drop the wire-format padding) so v0..v31 sit
188	  // contiguously and the Program-Buffer sweep can move 8 at a time via LMUL=8.
189	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
190	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
191	    std::memcpy(ram.data() + off + r * vlenb,
192	                state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX, vlenb);
193	}
194	
195	// Pack x1..x31 (8 bytes each) contiguously into the top kGprScratchBytes of the
196	// scratch page; the resume ld-sweep reads them back. state.gpr[1..31] is itself
197	// contiguous, so this is a single memcpy. Called before resume, gated by the
198	// caller on gpr_scratch_fits (the V region must leave room in the page).
199	inline void stage_gpr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
200	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram)
201	{
202	  const auto off =
203	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size()) + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes);
204	  std::memcpy(ram.data() + off, &state.gpr[1], 31 * 8);
205	}
206	
207	// Pack f0..f31 (8 bytes each) contiguously into the scratch page just below the
208	// GPR block; the resume fld-sweep reads them back. state.fpr[0..31] is itself
209	// contiguous, so this is a single memcpy. Called before resume, gated by the
210	// caller on fpr_scratch_fits (the V region must leave room for both blocks).
211	inline void stage_fpr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
212	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram)
213	{
214	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
215	                   + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes);
216	  std::memcpy(ram.data() + off, &state.fpr[0], 32 * 8);
217	}
218	
219	// Copy the span's top scratch page into state.vreg[]. Called inside the vsim
220	// drain path after the fixture's prologue vse8.v has settled the (possibly
221	// mutated) regfile bytes into RAM.
222	inline void read_v_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
223	                                std::span<const uint8_t> ram)
224	{
225	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
226	  // Unpack the vlenb-packed scratch back into the wire-strided vreg[] slots.
227	  // Each slot's padding (bytes vlenb..HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) is left as-is:
228	  // callers pass a passthrough state whose padding is already zero (the QEMU
229	  // drain zero-fills it), so the full 128-byte slots stay byte-identical to the
230	  // oracle that --verify compares against.
231	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
232	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
233	    std::memcpy(state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX,
234	                ram.data() + off + r * vlenb, vlenb);
235	}
236	
237	// Lift `count` GPRs (x1..x[count]) out of the scratch page into state.gpr[].
238	// Mirror of stage_gpr_to_scratch, reading from the identical top-of-page offset:
239	// the drain sd-sweep stored them here from the regfile. count is < 31 when the
240	// sweep's base register (itself a GPR) was captured separately via an abstract
241	// read and excluded from the sweep, so its slot must not be lifted.
242	inline void read_gpr_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
243	                                  std::span<const uint8_t> ram,
244	                                  std::size_t count)
245	{
246	  const auto off =
247	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size()) + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes);
248	  std::memcpy(&state.gpr[1], ram.data() + off, count * 8);
249	}
250	
251	// Lift f0..f31 out of the scratch page into state.fpr[]. Mirror of
252	// stage_fpr_to_scratch; the drain fsd-sweep stored them here. No f-reg is the
253	// sweep's base (that is an integer GPR), so all 32 round-trip.
254	inline void read_fpr_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
255	                                  std::span<const uint8_t> ram)
256	{
257	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
258	                   + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes);
259	  std::memcpy(&state.fpr[0], ram.data() + off, 32 * 8);
260	}
261	
262	// Pack the transported Andes+M-ext CSR values into the CSR scratch region (just
263	// below the FPR block) in canonical order; the resume csr_sweep ld's them into
264	// each CSR. Called before resume, gated per-CSR on flag + caps (for_each_sweep_
265	// csr), so an engine's unsupported CSRs never take a slot.
266	inline void stage_csr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
267	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram, const AndesCaps& caps)
268	{
269	  const auto base =
270	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
271	    + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes - kCsrScratchBytes);
272	  for_each_sweep_csr(state, caps,
273	    [&](std::size_t i, uint16_t /*addr*/, const uint64_t& value) {
274	      std::memcpy(ram.data() + base + i * 8, &value, 8);
275	    });
276	}
277	
278	// Lift the Andes+M-ext CSR values out of the CSR scratch region into state, the
279	// mirror of stage_csr_to_scratch: the drain csr_sweep sd'd them here. Same
280	// flag+caps-gated canonical order, so slot i lands in the field it came from.
281	inline void read_csr_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
282	                                  std::span<const uint8_t> ram,
283	                                  const AndesCaps& caps)
284	{
285	  const auto base =
286	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())
287	    + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes - kFprScratchBytes - kCsrScratchBytes);
288	  for_each_sweep_csr(state, caps,
289	    [&](std::size_t i, uint16_t /*addr*/, uint64_t& value) {
290	      std::memcpy(&value, ram.data() + base + i * 8, 8);
291	    });
292	}
293	
294	}  // namespace hybrid

1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <array>
17	#include <cstdint>
18	#include <cstdio>
19	#include <span>
20	#include <stdexcept>
21	#include <string>
22	
23	namespace hybrid {
24	
25	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
26	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
27	
28	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
29	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
30	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
31	
32	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
33	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
34	
35	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
36	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
37	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
38	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
39	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
40	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
42	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
43	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
44	
45	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
46	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
47	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
48	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
49	{
50	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
52	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
53	         | (0b111u << 12)
54	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
55	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
56	}
57	
58	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
59	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
60	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
61	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
62	{
63	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
64	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
65	         | (0b001u << 12)
66	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
67	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
68	}
69	
70	// Encode `csrrs rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=010). With rs1=x0 this is
71	// `csrr rd, csr`: a pure CSR read (the RISC-V spec suppresses the write side
72	// effect when rs1=x0). The CSR drain sweep reads each supported Andes/M-ext CSR
73	// into a temp GPR with this, then sd's it to the scratch page.
74	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrs(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
75	{
76	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
77	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
78	         | (0b010u << 12)
79	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
80	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
81	}
82	
83	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
84	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
85	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
86	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
87	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
88	{
89	    return (1u << 25)
90	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
91	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
92	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
93	}
94	
95	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
96	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
97	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
98	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
99	{
100	    return (1u << 25)
101	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
102	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
103	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
104	}
105	
106	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
107	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
108	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
109	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
110	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
111	{
112	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
113	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
114	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
115	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
116	}
117	
118	// Encode `ld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The GPR
119	// block-load sweeps x1..x31 from a scratch region addressed by a base register,
120	// so 31 abstract register writes collapse into a few Program-Buffer executions.
121	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_ld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
122	{
123	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
124	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
125	         | (0b011u << 12)
126	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
127	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
128	}
129	
130	// Encode `lwu rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=110 for 32-bit ZERO-
131	// extend). Same I-type shape as encode_ld but a word load: L2C MMIO registers
132	// must be accessed less than 8 bytes at a time (DS220 11.8.3), so the L2C
133	// config read-back loads a word. lwu (not lw) so a 32-bit register value does
134	// not sign-extend into the upper bits of the 64-bit GPR it lands in.
135	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_lwu(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
136	{
137	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
138	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
139	         | (0b110u << 12)
140	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
141	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
142	}
143	
144	// Encode `fld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD-FP opcode 0x07, funct3=011 for double). Same
145	// shape as encode_ld with the FP-load opcode: the FPR block-load sweeps f0..f31
146	// from the scratch region via an integer base register, collapsing 32 abstract
147	// FPR writes into a few Program-Buffer executions.
148	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
149	{
150	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
151	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
152	         | (0b011u << 12)
153	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
154	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
155	}
156	
157	// Encode `sd rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE opcode 0x23, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The
158	// mirror of encode_ld for the DRAIN direction: the GPR drain sweeps x1..x30 from
159	// the regfile INTO the scratch region via an integer base register, collapsing
160	// 31 abstract reads into a few Program-Buffer executions. S-type splits the
161	// signed 12-bit immediate: imm[11:5] -> bits 31:25, imm[4:0] -> bits 11:7.
162	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_sd(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
163	{
164	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
165	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
166	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
167	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
168	         | (0b011u << 12)
169	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
170	         | 0x23u;  // STORE opcode
171	}
172	
173	// Encode `sw rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE opcode 0x23, funct3=010 for 32-bit). Same
174	// S-type shape as encode_sd but a word store: L2C MMIO registers must be
175	// accessed less than 8 bytes at a time (DS220 11.8.3), so the L2C config restore
176	// writes a word. All documented L2C control bits live in the low 32 bits.
177	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_sw(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
178	{
179	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
180	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
181	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
182	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
183	         | (0b010u << 12)
184	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
185	         | 0x23u;  // STORE opcode
186	}
187	
188	// Encode `fsd rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE-FP opcode 0x27, funct3=011 for double).
189	// Same S-type shape as encode_sd with the FP-store opcode: the FPR drain sweeps
190	// f0..f31 from the regfile into the scratch region via an integer base register.
191	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fsd(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
192	{
193	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
194	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
195	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
196	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
197	         | (0b011u << 12)
198	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
199	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
200	}
201	
202	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
203	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
204	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
205	//
206	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
207	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
208	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
209	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
210	// surfacing the fault.
211	template<typename Bus>
212	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
213	{
214	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
215	        throw std::runtime_error(
216	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
217	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
218	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
219	
220	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
221	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
222	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
223	
224	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
225	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
226	
227	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
228	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
229	
230	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
231	    if (cmderr != 0u)
232	        throw std::runtime_error(
233	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
234	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
235	}
236	
237	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
238	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
239	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
240	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
241	
242	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
243	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
244	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
245	template<typename Bus>
246	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
247	{
248	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
249	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
250	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
251	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
252	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
253	                     "write_register_abstract");
254	}
255	
256	// Program-Buffer block sweep: seed integer base register `base_gpr` with
257	// `base_gpa`, then run `encode(reg, base_gpr, (reg-first_reg)*8)` for reg in
258	// [first_reg, last_reg) through the Program Buffer, batched at (progbufsize-1)
259	// instructions per execution (one slot reserved for the terminating ebreak).
260	// One uniform load/store encoder drives it, so the GPR/FPR restore (ld/fld,
261	// scratch -> regfile) and the GPR/FPR drain (sd/fsd, regfile -> scratch) share
262	// one implementation: ~32 registers move in ~6 halted-hart round-trips instead
263	// of ~32 abstract commands, and the values ride the shared scratch page, not
264	// DMI. The 8-byte-strided offset spans every slot (<= 248, within ld/sd's
265	// signed 12-bit immediate). The caller guarantees base_gpr is safe to seed: on
266	// a load it may be a swept register that rides LAST (its own load runs after
267	// every other use of it as the base); on a store it must be EXCLUDED from
268	// [first_reg, last_reg) -- seeding destroys its value before it could be stored
269	// -- and captured separately.
270	template<typename Bus>
271	inline void pb_block_sweep(Bus& bus, uint8_t base_gpr, uint64_t base_gpa,
272	                           uint8_t first_reg, uint8_t last_reg,
273	                           uint32_t (*encode)(uint8_t, uint8_t, int32_t))
274	{
275	    // The Program Buffer holds abstractcs.progbufsize entries (this DM reports
276	    // 8); reserve one slot for the terminating ebreak, so at most progbufsize-1
277	    // load/store insns per execution.
278	    const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) >> 24) & 0x1Fu;
279	    const std::size_t max_ops = (progbufsize > 1) ? progbufsize - 1u : 1u;
280	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(base_gpr), base_gpa);  // base pointer
281	    std::array<uint32_t, 32> batch{};
282	    std::size_t n = 0;
283	    for (uint8_t k = first_reg; k < last_reg; ++k) {
284	        batch[n++] = encode(k, base_gpr,
285	                            static_cast<int32_t>((k - first_reg) * 8));
286	        if (n == max_ops || k + 1 == last_reg) {
287	            exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), n});
288	            n = 0;
289	        }
290	    }
291	}
292	
293	// Direction for csr_sweep: Restore writes each CSR from the scratch page
294	// (ld + csrrw), Drain reads each CSR back to scratch (csrr + sd).
295	enum class CsrSweepDir { Restore, Drain };
296	
297	// Program-Buffer CSR sweep: transport a caps-supported list of CSRs between the
298	// hart and the scratch page. Unlike pb_block_sweep (one uniform ld/st per
299	// register), a CSR needs TWO instructions -- the CSR number is baked into the
300	// csrrw/csrr immediate, so it cannot be a runtime operand -- so this batches at
301	// (progbufsize-1)/2 CSRs per Program-Buffer execution:
302	//   Restore: ld val,(k*8)(base); csrrw x0, csrs[k], val   (scratch -> CSR)
303	//   Drain:   csrr val, csrs[k];  sd val,(k*8)(base)       (CSR -> scratch)
304	// `base` is an integer GPR seeded once with `base_gpa` (the CSR scratch region);
305	// `val` is a temp GPR the caller may clobber. The values ride the shared scratch
306	// page (staged/lifted by stage_csr_to_scratch / read_csr_from_scratch), not DMI.
307	// The csrs list is the caps-supported set in the SAME canonical order the host
308	// stager packs, so slot k*8 holds csrs[k]'s value. Empty list -> no-op (not even
309	// the base seed). The k*8 offset spans every slot (<= 81*8 = 648 < 2047).
310	//
311	// Every csrs[k] MUST be implemented by the target (the caller builds the list
312	// from caps): a csrrw/csrr to an unimplemented CSR raises cmderr and exec_progbuf
313	// throws, aborting the whole batch. That is intentional -- a faulting sweep means
314	// the caps map is wrong, a config bug to fix, not something to silently mirror.
315	// To make that bug FIXABLE, a faulting batch is re-run one CSR at a time and the
316	// thrown error names the offending CSR (re-running is safe: drain reads are
317	// idempotent, and a restore re-applies the same staged values).
318	template<typename Bus>
319	inline void csr_sweep(Bus& bus, uint8_t base_gpr, uint64_t base_gpa,
320	                      uint8_t val_gpr, std::span<const uint16_t> csrs,
321	                      CsrSweepDir dir)
322	{
323	    if (csrs.empty()) return;
324	    const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) >> 24) & 0x1Fu;
325	    // Two insns per CSR; reserve one slot for the terminating ebreak. Clamp to
326	    // the ebreak-adjusted payload cap so a batch never overruns the buffer.
327	    std::size_t usable = (progbufsize > 1) ? progbufsize - 1u : 1u;
328	    if (usable > kProgbufMaxInsns) usable = kProgbufMaxInsns;
329	    const std::size_t max_csrs = (usable >= 2) ? usable / 2u : 1u;
330	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(base_gpr), base_gpa);  // scratch base
331	    // The (transport; ld/sd) insn pair for csrs[k], shared by the batch build
332	    // and the fault bisect so both run the identical instructions.
333	    const auto pair_for = [&](std::size_t k) -> std::array<uint32_t, 2> {
334	        const int32_t off = static_cast<int32_t>(k * 8);
335	        if (dir == CsrSweepDir::Restore)
336	            return {encode_ld(val_gpr, base_gpr, off),
337	                    encode_csrrw(0, csrs[k], val_gpr)};
338	        return {encode_csrrs(val_gpr, csrs[k], 0),
339	                encode_sd(val_gpr, base_gpr, off)};
340	    };
341	    std::array<uint32_t, 32> batch{};
342	    std::size_t n = 0, in_batch = 0;
343	    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < csrs.size(); ++k) {
344	        const auto pair = pair_for(k);
345	        batch[n++] = pair[0];
346	        batch[n++] = pair[1];
347	        if (++in_batch == max_csrs || k + 1 == csrs.size()) {
348	            try {
349	                exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), n});
350	            } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
351	                for (std::size_t j = k + 1 - in_batch; j <= k; ++j) {
352	                    const auto one = pair_for(j);
353	                    try {
354	                        exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{one});
355	                    } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
356	                        char addr[8];
357	                        std::snprintf(addr, sizeof addr, "0x%x", csrs[j]);
358	                        throw std::runtime_error(
359	                            std::string{"csr_sweep: CSR "} + addr
360	                            + " raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR"
361	                              " the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)");
362	                    }
363	                }
364	                throw;  // no single CSR reproduced the batch fault
365	            }
366	            n = 0;
367	            in_batch = 0;
368	        }
369	    }
370	}
371	
372	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and the vlenb-packed
373	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
374	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
375	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m8 sets vl=8*vlenb and forces
376	// vstart=0, so one unit-stride access covers a whole LMUL=8 group of 8
377	// registers. Uses x5/x6 (vsetvl operands) and x7 (group base pointer) as
378	// scratch. `vlenb` is the runtime per-register width; the scratch must be
379	// packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so each 8-register group is
380	// contiguous.
381	template<typename Bus>
382	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t vlenb,
383	                            bool load)
384	{
385	    // The scratch holds v0..v31 packed contiguously at vlenb stride (see
386	    // stage_v_to_scratch), so 8 consecutive registers form one LMUL=8 group.
387	    // One vle8.v/vse8.v then moves a whole group (8*vlenb contiguous bytes,
388	    // vl=8*vlenb) and all 32 registers transfer in 4 grouped ops -- whose 4
389	    // (transfer; addi) pairs fit in a SINGLE Program-Buffer execution. Each PB
390	    // execution is one halted-hart DM round-trip (~1000 sim cycles in the
391	    // busy-poll), so this is the floor: one vsetvl + one grouped execution. The
392	    // register bytes never cross DMI; they ride the shared mmap.
393	    constexpr unsigned     kRegsPerGroup   = 8;  // LMUL=8
394	    // kVtypeE8M8's vlmul field (bits 2:0) must encode this LMUL, so one grouped
395	    // vle8.v/vse8.v really covers kRegsPerGroup registers (integer LMUL=1<<vlmul;
396	    // 0xC3 & 7 == 3 -> LMUL 8).
397	    static_assert((1u << (kVtypeE8M8 & 0x7u)) == kRegsPerGroup,
398	                  "kVtypeE8M8 must encode LMUL = kRegsPerGroup");
399	    constexpr std::size_t  kGroupSweepInsns = (32 / kRegsPerGroup) * 2;  // (ld;addi)*4
400	    static_assert(kGroupSweepInsns <= kProgbufMaxInsns,
401	                  "the grouped sweep must fit one Program Buffer execution");
402	    const uint64_t group_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(kRegsPerGroup) * vlenb;
403	    if (group_bytes > 2047)  // addi imm12 is signed 12-bit; max 8*128 = 1024
404	        throw std::runtime_error(
405	            "pb_v_data_sweep: 8*vlenb exceeds the addi imm12 range");
406	
407	    // vsetvl to e8/m8 with AVL = 8*vlenb sets vl = VLMAX = 8*vlenb (one
408	    // byte-element per lane across the whole group) and forces vstart = 0.
409	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), group_bytes);  // AVL
410	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M8);   // e8, m8, ta, ma
411	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
412	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
413	
414	    // Base pointer x7 staged once; the in-buffer addi advances it one group at
415	    // a time. The group base register must be LMUL-aligned: v0/v8/v16/v24.
416	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa);
417	    const uint32_t addi_step =
418	        encode_addi(7, 7, static_cast<int32_t>(group_bytes));
419	    std::array<uint32_t, kGroupSweepInsns> group_sweep{};
420	    std::size_t n = 0;
421	    for (uint8_t g = 0; g < 32; g += kRegsPerGroup) {
422	        group_sweep[n++] = load ? encode_vle8_v(g, 7) : encode_vse8_v(g, 7);
423	        group_sweep[n++] = addi_step;  // last group's addi is harmless dead work
424	    }
425	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{group_sweep.data(), n});
426	}
427	
428	}  // namespace hybrid

1	// Glues CsrTrigger and StateDrain. The simulator's run-loop calls on_retire
2	// once per committed PC; the controller decides via the trigger map whether
3	// to drain state and returns the populated hybrid_state_v1 if so. The
4	// caller (simulator.hpp) is responsible for writing the file and exiting
5	// with EXIT_HANDOFF_TO_QEMU.
6	
7	#pragma once
8	
9	#include "hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp"
10	#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"
11	#include "hybrid/resume_driver.hpp"
12	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
13	#include "hybrid/state_drain.hpp"
14	
15	#include <cstdint>
16	#include <optional>
17	#include <utility>
18	
19	namespace hybrid
20	{
21	
22	template<typename Trigger>
23	class HandoffController
24	{
25	public:
26	  // scratch_gpa (L26): forwarded to StateDrain for the V dump sweep; defaults
27	  // to the unset sentinel (non-V drains never read it). The simulator passes
28	  // the real mmap-top-page GPA. caps: the target core's Andes-CSR support,
29	  // forwarded to StateDrain so the drain re-read skips CSRs the core lacks.
30	  HandoffController(Trigger trigger, DmiBus& bus,
31	                    uint64_t scratch_gpa = kVScratchGpaUnset,
32	                    AndesCaps caps = AndesCaps::all())
33	      : trigger_{std::move(trigger)}, drain_{bus, scratch_gpa, caps}
34	  {}
35	
36	  // Snapshot of the QEMU 1 input state. When set, drain merges FP/CSR/V
37	  // fields from the snapshot into the freshly drained GPRs+PC, avoiding
38	  // a per-field DM Abstract Command on every handoff.
39	  void set_passthrough_input(hybrid_state_v1 input)
40	  {
41	    passthrough_ = input;
42	  }
43	
44	  // #1: when enabled, an EXIT drains only mcycle/minstret (StateDrain::
45	  // drain_counters_only) and passes every other field through from the
46	  // passthrough snapshot, instead of reading back the full register file. The
47	  // driver turns this on whenever --verify is off, where only the vsim mcycle
48	  // delta is consumed -- so the ~190 full-drain abstract commands are wasted.
49	  void set_minimal_drain(bool on)
50	  {
51	    minimal_drain_ = on;
52	  }
53	
54	  // Enable the drain-side PB block-store (dual of the resume block-load): the
55	  // GPR/FPR readback sweeps into the shared scratch page instead of per-register
56	  // Abstract Commands, and the Andes+M-ext CSR block rides a batched csrr+sd
57	  // sweep. The simulator lifts the swept bytes with read_{gpr,fpr,csr}_from_
58	  // scratch after on_retire returns.
59	  //
60	  // The CSR sweep is safe on the drain side because a `csrr` of a CSR the hart
61	  // implements never faults, and the caps table is exact -- the one over-claimed
62	  // CSR (mcountermask_m 0x7D1, whose csrr raised cmderr on the M-only premium
63	  // and aborted the whole batch) is UMODE-gated now. The RESTORE sweep stays
64	  // off: a csrrw can still fault on read-only/WARL-illegal fields (see the
65	  // simulator's resume NOTE).
66	  void set_block_store_drain(bool on)
67	  {
68	    drain_.set_gpr_block_store(on);
69	    drain_.set_fpr_block_store(on);
70	    drain_.set_csr_sweep(on);
71	  }
72	
73	  // v5: forward the engine's L2C presence + MMIO base to the exit drain, so it
74	  // re-reads the writable L2C config registers for --verify (dual of the resume
75	  // side's set_l2c). Off unless the engine has an L2C.
76	  void set_l2c(bool present, uint64_t base) { drain_.set_l2c(present, base); }
77	
78	  // Read-only view of the underlying trigger. Used by the ROI kanata-gate
79	  // derivation, which needs to read scanned EXIT PCs without consuming them.
80	  auto trigger() const -> const Trigger& { return trigger_; }
81	
82	  auto on_retire(uint64_t pc) -> std::optional<hybrid_state_v1>
83	  {
84	    if constexpr (requires { trigger_.observe_commit(); }) {
85	      trigger_.observe_commit();
86	    }
87	    const auto hit = trigger_.lookup(pc);
88	    // Only EXIT drains; entry is QEMU's job, vsim ignores ENTER.
89	    if (!hit || hit->kind != HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT)
90	      return std::nullopt;
91	    if (passthrough_)
92	      return minimal_drain_ ? drain_.drain_counters_only(*passthrough_)
93	                            : drain_.drain_with_passthrough(*passthrough_);
94	    return drain_.drain();
95	  }
96	
97	private:
98	  Trigger trigger_;
99	  StateDrain drain_;
100	  std::optional<hybrid_state_v1> passthrough_;
101	  bool minimal_drain_ = false;
102	};
103	
104	}  // namespace hybrid

option(VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID "Enable hybrid QEMU+Verilator co-simulation" OFF)

function(hybrid_add_test name source)

4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

# DM Abstract-Command coverage (vsim)

The hybrid handoff drives architectural state into the running RTL via the
in-process JTAG/DTM and the RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands. This page
records which `regno` ranges actually round-trip on each CPU variant.

A `MISS` row blocks the handoff for that field: either add a Program Buffer
or DPI fallback, or drop the field from the v1 ABI.

## How to populate this table

```bash
# in one terminal
./build/sim_ax45mpv_premium --jtag-port 9104 hello.elf

# in another terminal
openocd -f hybrid/scripts/test_dm_coverage.tcl 2>&1 \
  | tee /tmp/dm_coverage.log
```

Then translate the log into the table below.

## Coverage matrix

| Group              | Regnos              | Blocking? | ax45mpv_premium | ax66 | d45 |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | --------- | --------------- | ---- | --- |
| GPR x0..x31        | 0x1000-0x101F       | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| FPR f0..f31        | 0x1020-0x103F       | yes (FP)  | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mstatus            | 0x300               | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mepc/mtvec/mcause  | 0x341/0x305/0x342   | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mtval/mscratch     | 0x343/0x340         | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| medeleg/mideleg    | 0x302/0x303         | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mip/mie            | 0x344/0x304         | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mcycle/minstret    | 0xB00/0xB02         | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| satp               | 0x180               | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| pmpcfg0..15        | 0x3A0-0x3AF         | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| pmpaddr0..63       | 0x3B0-0x3EF         | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| V scalar CSRs      | 0x008,0xC20-0xC22   | no (V)    | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| V regfile v0..v31  | (no abstract regno) | no (V)    | n/a (PB)        | -    | -   |
| Andes mmsc_cfg     | 0xFC2               | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| Andes mmisc_ctl    | 0x7D0               | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| Andes mcache_ctl   | 0x7CA               | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |

`PB` = Program Buffer fallback required (no abstract-regno path).
`Blocking?` = MISS on this row prevents the handoff from being correct without
a fallback.

`ResumeDriver` (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) writes every CSR row in this
table -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block --
with one Abstract Command per CSR, gated by the LG1 liveness check. There is
no Program-Buffer CSR sweep on restore: a `csrrw` to a caps-supported but
read-only / WARL-illegal CSR raises `cmderr`, and a batched Program-Buffer
program can't recover from a fault partway through without corrupting the
rest of the batch, whereas the abstract path's per-CSR `clear_cmderr` just
tolerates that one CSR and moves on to the next. Only the GPR, FPR, and V
data-register blocks (plus V's `vtype`/`vl` Tier-B `vsetvl`) use the Program
Buffer on restore.

The **drain** side is different and unaffected: `StateDrain`'s Andes+M-ext
CSR sweep (`set_csr_sweep`, on by default) stays on the Program Buffer,
because a `csrr` read never faults the way a `csrrw` write can, so a batched
read sweep is safe.

content.text:
對,但只有 restore 端是 Abstract command。CSR 分兩個方向:

- **Restore(resume 端)**: 全部 abstract,一個 CSR 一次 write,沒有 PB sweep。原因:`csrrw` 寫到 read-only/WARL CSR 會 fault,batch 到一半 fault 沒法像 per-CSR 的 cmderr-clear 那樣容忍單一失敗。
- **Drain(exit 端)**: Andes+M-ext CSR block **還是走 PB sweep**(`StateDrain::drain_andes_m_ext` -> `csrr x5, csr; sd x5, slot(x6)`,simulator 開 `set_csr_sweep(true)`)。`csrr` 讀永遠不會 fault,所以 batch 是安全的,~82 個 CSR 幾個 PB execution 就讀完,不用 82 次 abstract read。

那塊 656-byte 的 CSR scratch 區就是給 **drain sweep** 落地用的:sweep 把每個 CSR 值 `sd` 進 scratch,host 端再用 `read_csr_from_scratch` 撈進 `hybrid_state_v1`。

這次移除的只有 GPR/FPR 的 sweep;drain 端 CSR sweep 本來就在、也刻意保留(這是你之前定的設計,CLAUDE.md 有記錄:"the drain side's CSR sweep is unaffected, since a `csrr` read never faults the way a `csrrw` write can")。要一起拔掉改全 abstract 也可以,但 drain 端會多 ~80 次 DM round-trip(每次數百 simulated cycles)-- 不過那是 exit 之後的事,不影響 ROI 的 cycle 數字。

**1. sweep 用在哪?** 兩個地方:
- **Exit drain**: 只在 `--verify` 開的時候跑。verify 關掉時 driver 會傳 `--drain-minimal`(`cmd_run.cpp:463`),drain 只讀 mcycle/minstret 兩個 counter,CSR sweep 根本不會執行 -- 因為沒人要看那些欄位。

**2. 可以改用 abstract command 嗎?** 可以,隨時可以:
- `StateDrain::drain_andes_m_ext` 本來就有 abstract fallback(sweep 關掉或 V 塞滿 page 時,就一個 CSR 一次 abstract read),讀出來的欄位完全一樣。

# DM Abstract-Command coverage (vsim)

The hybrid handoff drives architectural state into the running RTL via the
in-process JTAG/DTM and the RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands. This page
records which `regno` ranges actually round-trip on each CPU variant.

A `MISS` row blocks the handoff for that field: either add a Program Buffer
or DPI fallback, or drop the field from the v1 ABI.

## How to populate this table

```bash
# in one terminal
./build/sim_ax45mpv_premium --jtag-port 9104 hello.elf

# in another terminal
openocd -f hybrid/scripts/test_dm_coverage.tcl 2>&1 \
  | tee /tmp/dm_coverage.log
```

Then translate the log into the table below.

## Coverage matrix

| Group              | Regnos              | Blocking? | ax45mpv_premium | ax66 | d45 |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | --------- | --------------- | ---- | --- |
| GPR x0..x31        | 0x1000-0x101F       | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| FPR f0..f31        | 0x1020-0x103F       | yes (FP)  | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mstatus            | 0x300               | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mepc/mtvec/mcause  | 0x341/0x305/0x342   | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mtval/mscratch     | 0x343/0x340         | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| medeleg/mideleg    | 0x302/0x303         | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mip/mie            | 0x344/0x304         | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| mcycle/minstret    | 0xB00/0xB02         | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| satp               | 0x180               | yes       | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| pmpcfg0..15        | 0x3A0-0x3AF         | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| pmpaddr0..63       | 0x3B0-0x3EF         | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| V scalar CSRs      | 0x008,0xC20-0xC22   | no (V)    | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| V regfile v0..v31  | (no abstract regno) | no (V)    | n/a (PB)        | -    | -   |
| Andes mmsc_cfg     | 0xFC2               | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| Andes mmisc_ctl    | 0x7D0               | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |
| Andes mcache_ctl   | 0x7CA               | no        | TBD             | TBD  | TBD |

`PB` = Program Buffer fallback required (no abstract-regno path).
`Blocking?` = MISS on this row prevents the handoff from being correct without
a fallback.

## Restore-side CSR policy: Abstract Command only, no batching

`ResumeDriver` (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) writes every CSR row in this
table -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block --
with one Abstract Command per CSR, gated by the LG1 liveness check. There is
no Program-Buffer CSR sweep on restore: a `csrrw` to a caps-supported but
read-only / WARL-illegal CSR raises `cmderr`, and a batched Program-Buffer
program can't recover from a fault partway through without corrupting the
rest of the batch, whereas the abstract path's per-CSR `clear_cmderr` just
tolerates that one CSR and moves on to the next. GPRs and FPRs likewise
restore (and drain) via one Abstract Command per register. Only the V
data-register block (plus V's `vtype`/`vl` Tier-B `vsetvl`) and the L2C MMIO
window use the Program Buffer on restore.

The **drain** side is different and unaffected: `StateDrain`'s Andes+M-ext
CSR sweep (`set_csr_sweep`, on by default) stays on the Program Buffer,
because a `csrr` read never faults the way a `csrrw` write can, so a batched
read sweep is safe.

This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

### 4.4 Verifying a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

With the QEMU2 handback removed, the code after your ROI never runs, so a
hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(default OFF) cross-checks the run's correctness:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify your_prog.elf
# ...
# [marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
# [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
# [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

Performance note: without `--verify`, the vsim leg drains only `mcycle`/`minstret`
(the cycle figure) and skips reading back the full architectural register file
over the Debug Module. On a full drain the GPR and FPR readback ride
Program-Buffer sweeps into the shared scratch page (like the vector-register

M-mode CSRs, whose simulated debug cycles dominate hybrid wall-clock for a short
ROI but never affect the cycle count. `--verify` needs every field for the diff,
so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to take noticeably longer

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build this repo's vsim inside the Dockerfile's env-stage container image.
#
# What it does (README Option 3):
#   1. Build the `env` target image (verilator + toolchain) from ./Dockerfile.
#   2. Run ./build.sh inside that container with the repo bind-mounted at /work,
#      so build artifacts land in ./build/ on the host.
#
# Trim config.yaml to the CPU(s) you need first to cut build time.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Container runtime: prefer podman, fall back to docker.
if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=podman
elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=docker
else
  echo "error: need podman or docker on PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "error: missing $ROOT/Dockerfile" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# build.sh / cmake pull in external/ submodules; bail early if they are empty.
if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/external/fmt/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
  echo "error: submodules not initialized - run:" >&2
  echo "  git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT"

"$RUNTIME" build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
"$RUNTIME" run --rm \
  -v "$ROOT:/work" \
  -w /work localhost/vsim-env:latest ./build.sh

#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
# VSIM_QEMU); fall back to the legacy in-tree build only if it is unset.
VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}

require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

content.content:
1	---
2	name: csr-transport-bringup
3	description: >
4	  Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given
5	  the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole
6	  pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence
7	  conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions,
8	  bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the
9	  Program-Buffer CSR sweep, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill
10	  whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport /
11	  transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value
12	  table, which mode a CSR is supported in, csr_sweep cmderr faults, or
13	  --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say
14	  "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine
15	  test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or
16	  adding a new config of an existing core.
17	---
18	
19	# CSR transport bring-up for a new Andes core
20	
21	Inputs you need from the user (ask if missing):
22	- The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family (the repo carries
23	  `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` for the current cores).
24	- The engine name (e.g. `ax45mpv_premium`) and a built vsim checkout
25	  (`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env` points at its `build/`).
26	- Optionally the matching QEMU `-cpu` name for the oracle leg.
27	
28	The goal: every CSR the core implements and the ROI can touch is restored at
29	resume, re-read at drain, and `--verify`-compared -- and every CSR the core
30	does NOT implement is gated off, because the batched Program-Buffer sweep
31	faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR.
32	
33	Work in this order. Each phase has a reference file with the details --
34	read it when you reach the phase, not before.
35	
36	## Phase 0: establish ground truth (three sources)
37	
38	Validation means connecting THREE sources per CSR -- the spec, the build
39	config, and the CPU core RTL -- and they speak different languages:
40	- CONFIG: `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (the BUILD copy -- the
41	  `external/` source tree can differ) + `sim_<engine> --describe`.
42	- RTL: the CSR decoder's `existent_csr` equation (kv_core family:
43	  `andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_csr_dec.v`). This is the Rosetta stone: it
44	  states each spec existence condition as a function of config params --
45	  the mapping neither document contains.
46	- SPEC: Phase 1 below.
47	Read `references/three-way-audit.md` -- the tutorial for connecting the
48	three and turning the result into the engine's test cases. Do not trust
49	QEMU: its gdbstub exposes CSRs the vsim RTL does not implement, and
50	restoring or sweeping one of those stalls or faults the Debug Module.
51	
52	## Phase 1: mine the spec
53	
54	Run `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf>` to refresh
55	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (needs PyMuPDF; use a venv). Then pull,
56	for each CSR the core claims: the IM Requirement (existence condition), the
57	Access Mode, and the reset value. The SPA has a fixed per-CSR layout and a
58	consolidated existence table (Table 13) -- see
59	`references/spec-mining.md` for the exact headers and extraction recipes.
60	
61	## Phase 2: classify dispositions

---
name: csr-transport-bringup
description: >
  Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given
  the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole
  pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence
  conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions,
  bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the
  Program-Buffer CSR sweep, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill
  whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport /
  transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value
  table, which mode a CSR is supported in, csr_sweep cmderr faults, or
  --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say
  "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine
  test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or
  adding a new config of an existing core.
---

# CSR transport bring-up for a new Andes core

Inputs you need from the user (ask if missing):
- The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family (the repo carries
  `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` for the current cores).
- The engine name (e.g. `ax45mpv_premium`) and a built vsim checkout
  (`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env` points at its `build/`).
- Optionally the matching QEMU `-cpu` name for the oracle leg.

The goal: every CSR the core implements and the ROI can touch is restored at
resume, re-read at drain, and `--verify`-compared -- and every CSR the core
does NOT implement is gated off, because the batched Program-Buffer sweep
faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR.

Work in this order. Each phase has a reference file with the details --
read it when you reach the phase, not before.

## Phase 0: establish ground truth (three sources)

Validation means connecting THREE sources per CSR -- the spec, the build
config, and the CPU core RTL -- and they speak different languages:
- CONFIG: `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (the BUILD copy -- the
  `external/` source tree can differ) + `sim_<engine> --describe`.
- RTL: the CSR decoder's `existent_csr` equation (kv_core family:
  `andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_csr_dec.v`). This is the Rosetta stone: it
  states each spec existence condition as a function of config params --
  the mapping neither document contains.
- SPEC: Phase 1 below.
Read `references/three-way-audit.md` -- the tutorial for connecting the
three and turning the result into the engine's test cases. Do not trust
QEMU: its gdbstub exposes CSRs the vsim RTL does not implement, and
restoring or sweeping one of those stalls or faults the Debug Module.

## Phase 1: mine the spec

Run `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf>` to refresh
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (needs PyMuPDF; use a venv). Then pull,
for each CSR the core claims: the IM Requirement (existence condition), the
Access Mode, and the reset value. The SPA has a fixed per-CSR layout and a
consolidated existence table (Table 13) -- see
`references/spec-mining.md` for the exact headers and extraction recipes.

## Phase 2: classify dispositions

Run `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` and
the guard `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`. The guard enforces
inventory == matrix == ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`), so a CSR added to
the wire format without a disposition (or vice versa) fails loudly. New
transported CSRs are one X-macro line in `state_abi.h`
(`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`); every consumer
(plugin drain, restore, drain re-read, verify) iterates the same list.

## Phase 3: bind capability gates

For each transported CSR, build the three-way translation row (spec
condition <-> RTL `existent_csr` term <-> config macros; see
`references/three-way-audit.md`), then encode it: a gate in the vsim repo's
`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (address -> gate), the `_NDS_*` binding in
`andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as "off" -- never a compile
error), and the same rule in the andesim mirror
`scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py` (the parity guard keeps the two
honest). The gate must encode the RTL's existence term, not a
plausibly-related feature; three real bugs came from getting this wrong
(0x7D1, jvt, 0x7CF/PMNDS). Follow TDD: model the new engine's config shape
as a caps helper in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` and write the
failing expectation first. Read `references/caps-gating.md` -- it carries
the gate-authoring rules and the write-prerequisite (setup ordering)
requirements.

## Phase 4: reset values and verify exclusions

Two reset-value sources exist and they legitimately differ:
- The SPA reset table (documentation; many fields are IM = implementation
  determined or DC = don't care).
- The EMPIRICAL baseline the simulator drains from the freshly reset hart
  (cached per engine build + ELF). The liveness gate compares against this
  one -- it is self-truthing, so spec IM/DC values need no manual table.

Where QEMU's reset differs from the engine's reset for a CSR the program
never writes (e.g. `msp_bound`, `milmb` enable bit), a strict compare
false-positives: add it to `andes_verify_excluded` in
`driver/state_diff.cpp` with a comment naming the divergence. Do NOT
exclude a CSR to hide a transport bug -- exclusion is only for
engine-implementation artifacts.

## Phase 5: validate (the ladder)

Run bottom-up; each rung catches what the one below cannot. The key
insight: the tolerant abstract path MASKS capability bugs (a faulting read
mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, --verify falsely matches), so only
the batched CSR sweep truly validates the caps table -- it faults on an
over-claim and bisects to NAME the offending CSR. A cold-cache hybrid run
exercises it via the baseline capture. Full commands, expected outputs, and
failure playbook: `references/validation.md`.

## Phase 6: register the engine (per-engine test completeness)

andesim is a commercial product: every supported engine BUILD must ship its
own complete, machine-checked CSR test artifacts -- and a rebuild of the
same core with a different config counts as a NEW registration (the
config.inc hash is the identity, so reuse is impossible by construction).
Four deliverables per engine build: the CSR manifest (every spec CSR:
implemented? transported? why? empirical reset value), a BOTH-direction
completeness check (over-claims fault the sweep; under-claims -- implemented
but not transported and not on a named exclusion -- must fail a script, not
a human's memory), generated per-engine write-survival fixtures, and a
registration guard so an unregistered engine fails loudly. Read
`references/engine-registration.md` for the contract, the file layout, and
the recipes (including what to build the first time the tooling is missing).

## Phase 7: commit and document

TDD and Tidy First apply: caps fixes, sweep/transport changes, and docs are
separate commits, each on a green suite. Update the vsim `ROADMAP.md`
known-limits and `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (section 4.4 documents what --verify
compares). Update `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv` through the classifier,
never by hand -- the guard checks policy == matrix.

23	```
24

27	matrix that the classifier policy does not reproduce.

30

34	  --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
35	```
36	
37	The capture is a FULL drain of the freshly reset hart and its CSR block
38	rides the batched PB sweep over the COMPLETE caps-supported list -- so a
39	clean capture empirically proves every claimed CSR is csrr-able on this
40	RTL. One over-claim aborts the run with the bisected name:
41	
42	```

44	map over-claims a CSR the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)
45	```
46	
47	Fix the named CSR's gate (see caps-gating.md), rebuild, rerun; repeat
48	until the capture is clean. Expect the `--verify` field count to DROP by
49	one per de-claimed CSR (e.g. premium went 146 -> 144 when 0x7D1 and 0x017
50	left the set) -- a drop is correct, those fields were zero-vs-zero
51	false matches before.
52	
53	Read the error TEXT as a discriminator: the CSR sweep bisects its batch
54	faults and rethrows a RENAMED error (`csr_sweep: CSR 0x...`). So a raw
55	`exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3` means the fault is in one of
56	the NON-CSR Program-Buffer sites instead: the FPR/V data sweeps with
57	mstatus.FS/VS still Off (flags claim FP/V the engine lacks -- check the
58	QEMU-side ISA pairing), or a load/store access fault on the scratch page
59	(memory map does not cover mmap top page). On sim binaries older than the

72	  hide a transport bug.

88	engine and take ~80 s each.

91	
92	Every Debug-Module operation (abstract command or PB exec) costs ~200-900
93	SIMULATED cycles at ~10 kHz wall speed, so full-drain wall-clock is
94	dominated by DM op COUNT, not bytes:
95	- GPR/FPR: PB block sweeps, ~6 round-trips each instead of 31/32 ops.
96	- Andes+M-ext CSRs: batched csrr+sd sweep, 3 CSRs per PB exec (progbufsize

102	  (`--no-reset-baseline` to disable; the cache key includes the sim
103	  binary's mtime+size, so rebuilds self-invalidate).
104

111	  without a lift silently loses in-ROI CSR writes.
112	- Scratch page layout (top page of RAM): V data grows up from the base;
113	  GPR block at the top, FPR below it, CSR block below that. Every user is
114	  fits-gated on the live vlenb so a full V page falls back to abstract

1	# Capability gating: mapping IM Requirements to engine gates
2	
3	Three files, three roles (all in the vsim repo):
4	
5	| File | Role |
6	|------|------|
7	| `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` | CSR address -> `AndesGate` (spec knowledge, engine-free, unit-testable) |
8	| `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp` | `AndesGate` -> `_NDS_*` config macro (the one binding site) |
9	| `build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` | what THIS engine actually has (ground truth) |
10	
11	A CSR with no case in `andes_gate_for` defaults to ALWAYS = transported
12	unconditionally. Every CSR added to the ABI lists therefore needs a
13	deliberate decision: ALWAYS only for base machine CSRs every Andes core
14	has (mxstatus, mclk_ctl, mdcause).
15	
16	## The rules (each one paid for by a real bug)
17	
18	1. **Gate on the RTL's existence term, exactly -- compound conditions get
19	   compound (derived) gates.** Not on a feature that usually comes along
20	   with it, and never on HALF the condition. `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1)
21	   exists when `(mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1)`; it was first gated
22	   PERF_MONITOR (missing the privilege half -- faulted on M-only premium),
23	   then UMODE (missing the scheme half -- would over-claim on a U-mode
24	   Sscofpmf core). The RTL term is `PERF & !SSCOFPMF & multi_level_mode`,
25	   so the gate is the derived conjunction `PMNDS_UMODE`, computed once at
26	   the binding site (`andes_caps_config.hpp`) from the macros. When a
27	   condition spans several knobs, add a derived gate named after the SPEC
28	   concept (PMNDS) and document the RTL term next to it.
29	
30	2. **A standard-extension CSR is not implied by its Andes-classic
31	   sibling.** `jvt` (0x017) is Zcmt's table-jump base; classic Andes
32	   CoDense is `exec.it` + `uitb` (0x800). Gating jvt on CODENSE faulted the
33	   sweep on every CoDense core. When no config.inc knob exists for an
34	   extension, add the gate anyway bound to the macro it WOULD be
35	   (`_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT`): absent reads as off today, and a future
36	   config turns it on without a code change.
37	
38	3. **The tolerant abstract path masks over-claims -- do not trust a passing
39	   --verify as caps validation.** `read_register_64` clears a faulting
40	   read and mirrors it as zero; QEMU drains zero for a CSR the program
41	   never wrote; `--verify` matches zero == zero. Both bugs above were
42	   "verified" for months. The batched PB `csr_sweep` is the real
43	   validator: one over-claimed CSR faults the whole batch, and the sweep
44	   bisects to name it:
45	   `csr_sweep: CSR 0x17 raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR
46	   the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)`.
47	
48	4. **QEMU-exposes != vsim-implements.** QEMU's `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` models
49	   full M+S+U and its gdbstub advertises CSRs the M-only RTL lacks.
50	   Capability is decided from vsim's config.inc, never from what QEMU
51	   drains. (To dump what QEMU really exposes: RSP
52	   `qXfer:features:read:riscv-csr.xml`.)
53	
54	## TDD recipe for a caps change
55	
56	1. RED: in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`, model the engine's
57	   config.inc shape as a helper (see `premium()`) -- set exactly the gates
58	   its `_NDS_*` macros turn on. Assert the expected `supports_csr()`
59	   verdicts, including the one that currently fails. Run in the vsim build
60	   container; show the failure.
61	2. GREEN: move/add the `case` in `andes_gate_for` (and the binding in
62	   `andes_caps_config.hpp` if the gate is new). Comment the spec condition.
63	3. Rebuild the sim target and rerun; then climb the validation ladder.
64	
65	Keep the test helper honest: if the engine's config changed (or was
66	mis-modeled, as premium's perf monitor once was), fix the helper to match
67	`config.inc` -- the helper IS the machine-checked record of the engine
68	shape.
69	
70	## Write requirements: what must be true before a restore can SET a CSR
71	
72	Existence is only half of "can we set it". The restore path has ordering
73	prerequisites -- violating them writes values the hart drops or faults:
74	
75	- `mstatus.FS`/`VS` must be non-Off before any FPR/V access (fld/vle8
76	  sweeps AND abstract FPR/V-CSR ops raise illegal-instruction at reset,
77	  where both are Off). Resume and the baseline capture both enable them
78	  first.
79	- `vtype`/`vl` are restorable only via `vsetvl` (direct vtype write sets
80	  vill; vl is read-only); `vstart` must be written AFTER vsetvl (vsetvl
81	  zeroes it); the V-data sweep's own vsetvl clobbers all three, so
82	  architectural V-CSR restore runs after the data sweep.
83	- `mcounterwen` gates which counter-mask writes take effect: restore the
84	  write-enable before the counters it enables. `msp_bound`/`msp_base`
85	  before `mhsp_ctl` (enabling stack-safe with stale bounds traps).
86	- WARL fields silently pin: after a write that MUST take (e.g. `dcsr.prv`),
87	  read back and verify, and abort with a pick-another-engine error if
88	  pinned.
89	- The restore-side CSR sweep stays OFF: a `csrrw` to a read-only or
90	  WARL-illegal field faults the batch, and unlike the drain there is no
91	  idempotent retry story for partially-applied writes. Restores go through
92	  the per-CSR tolerant abstract path until a per-CSR writability model
93	  exists.

35	(csr_addr == 12'h7d1) & (PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT == 1) & (SSCOFPMF_SUPPORT == 0) & multi_level_mode
36	(csr_addr == 12'h017) & (ZCE_SUPPORT_INT == 1)
37	(csr_addr == 12'h7c5) & (POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT == 1)

```sh
# andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_csr_dec.v
grep -o "(csr_addr == 12'h7cf)[^|]*" .../kv_csr_dec.v
```
